header.stance: 通膨使聯準會更接近升息

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 核心通膨意外偏強，聯準會更接近升息

核心通膨高於預期，使市場幾乎完全反映聯準會9月升息，美債曲線週五趨平；油價回落則幫助長端收復部分失地。2年期殖利率上升7個基點至4.63%，10年期上升1個基點至4.96%，30年期下降2個基點至5.35%。整週而言，2年期仍上升26個基點，10年期上升18個基點。

這次通膨意外並非全面加速，卻也難以忽略。核心CPI月增0.3%，高於預估的0.2%；行動通訊費用創紀錄上漲，其他服務價格也走強。密西根大學調查隨後顯示，消費者信心下降的同時，通膨預期反而升高。期貨反映的9月升息機率由約70%升至90%，年底前則已反映兩次升息。

長端的定價沒有同樣悲觀。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4個基點至2.36%，實質殖利率則上升5個基點至2.60%。油價回落支持股市，美國投資級及高收益債利差也小幅收窄。融資需求仍能找到買方，可轉換證券發行創紀錄，三菱日聯銀行資本債的定價利差也比前次更窄；但South East Water仍未能與投資人就價格取得共識。

週末的新攻擊與沙烏地管線持續停擺，隨後讓週一亞洲盤的油價重新上漲。週五市場原本因原油回落、預期聯準會更積極回應通膨而稍獲喘息，接下來的政策會議卻又面臨新的供應威脅。

## 核心月增率的意外，壓過年增率下降的利多

8月整體CPI月增0.4%，符合路透調查預估，高於7月的0.1%；年增率維持3.4%，也符合預期。核心CPI月增0.3%，高於預估及7月的0.2%，但年增率仍由2.5%降至2.4%。

能源價格上漲2.1%，食品雜貨近乎持平，屋主設算租金增加0.2%。較令市場不安的是，排除能源與租金的服務價格上漲0.5%。行動通訊費用出現歷來最大漲幅，旅館、汽車旅館及機票價格也明顯上升。核心商品僅增加0.1%，主要來自新車與中古車。通訊費用或可解釋部分一次性影響，但漲價並不只集中於此。

科技相關價格的年增幅也突出：軟體與配件上漲25.4%，創歷史新高，電腦、周邊及智慧家庭助理設備上漲8.4%，接近紀錄。資料中心投資熱潮的成本壓力，也開始反映在消費物價上。另一方面，實質平均時薪較2025年8月下降0.3%，家庭購買力仍受擠壓。

密西根大學9月消費者信心初值由51.7降至47.8，低於路透調查預估的51.0。一年期通膨預期由4.0%跳升至4.6%，五年期由3.3%升至3.4%，高於2024年的2.8%至3.2%區間。調查主持人Joanne Hsu指出，燃料價格與貿易緊張推高預期。彭博分析顯示，共和黨支持者的信心，已回吐川普2024年勝選後的大部分改善；自2023年以來，也首次有過半消費者預期未來12個月利率會上升。

2年期殖利率最初升至4.66%，長端隨後回穩，使2年與10年期利差收窄6個基點至33個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄9個基點至72個基點。BMO的Ian Lyngen認為，短端下跌、長端走強，反映市場重新相信聯準會會處理通膨。摩根資產管理的Priya Misra則指出，數據公布前，價格已納入不少溫和升息循環的預期。

經濟學家的預測仍隨新資料調整。TD Securities放棄2026年全年不變的看法，改估9月將是三次升息中的第一次；摩根大通與Nationwide也轉向近期升息。Nationwide的Kathy Bostjancic擔心，石油、汽油與柴油漲價會傳到其他價格及通膨預期。Evercore ISI的Krishna Guha與團隊認為，數據不夠有利，Kevin Warsh若再忽略一次能源衝擊，可能傷及政策公信力。

這與CPI公布前的調查形成明顯差距。彭博9月4日至9日訪問的48名經濟學家中，只有13人預估本月升息，多數認為利率將維持至2027年底。Conference Board的Yelena Shulyatyeva原先不升息的預測，也明確以通膨沒有顯著加速為前提，週五數據改變了這項判斷基礎。

白宮訊息在收盤後也有變化。川普週日再次表示，美國應享有全球最低利率，並稱不清楚聯準會是否會升息，也重申未來可能陸續實施更多貿易限制。Kevin Hassett週五曾說，升息會引來總統回應；週日接受CNN訪問時，則表示白宮會支持委員會決策。他在Fox News Sunday另稱，川普可能不高興，但會維護Warsh的獨立性。

## 週五油價回落，週末出口管線風險卻再升高

週五債市收盤時，布蘭特原油下跌2.81%至$104.61，WTI下跌2.37%至$100.05。波灣國家可能與伊朗就荷姆茲海峽進行談判，加上IEA下修需求預測，帶來短暫利多。美股在連跌四天後反彈，S&P 500上漲0.86%、Nasdaq 100上漲0.91%、半導體指數上漲1.81%，VIX下跌11.21%至15.84。不過，布蘭特整週仍上漲8.65%，WTI上漲9.37%。

IEA同時下修供給與需求。機構目前預估2026年全球供給每日減少570萬桶、約6%，先前估計約減少4%。8月庫存以每日310萬桶的速度下降，降至2023年以來低點。沙烏地每日供給減少230萬桶至600萬桶，創逾三十年最低，OPEC+每日產量則減少180萬桶至3,880萬桶。波灣供應全面恢復的時間，被延後至2027年。

消費端也正在適應昂貴、短缺的燃料。IEA將2026年每日需求降幅由160萬桶擴大至250萬桶，尤其柴油高價正在壓抑使用量。AAA統計的美國柴油均價週五達每加侖$6.0556，創歷史紀錄。公路卡車運輸約占柴油消費三分之二，成本可直接傳至運費。烏克蘭攻擊減少俄羅斯柴油出口，中東煉油設施也仍在修復；即使取得原油，加工瓶頸也未必解除。

亞洲燃料補貼可能把部分負擔轉向政府。Emkay的Madhavi Arora估計，布蘭特每上漲$10，理論上會使印度通膨增加35個基點、成長減少15個基點，但本次供應來源較分散，敏感度可能較低。泰國法政大學的Puree Sirasoontorn估計，石油基金赤字可能由THB830億增至約THB1,000億，必要時須由政府借款支應；這些仍是風險估計，並非已發生的支出。

週末沙烏地東西向管線仍未恢復。這條繞過荷姆茲海峽、通往延布的路線，原本每日運送約400萬桶。買家與交易員向路透表示，若持續停擺，可能移除全球多達4%的供給。三名業界人士估計，延布庫存只能再支應五至七天出口；修復預估則不一致，有人估五至六週，也有人認為可較早恢復部分輸送。

沙烏地官媒報導，胡塞武裝再度攻擊吉贊與鄰近軍事基地。荷姆茲海峽一艘船遭投射物擊中起火，船員撤離；伊朗另稱，一艘伊朗商船上有一人死亡、四人受傷。阿曼外交部長Badr Albusaidi表示，原定週一舉行的波灣與伊朗會談已延期，臨時航道的討論因此仍未有結果。

格林威治時間週日22:14、即週一亞洲早盤，布蘭特上漲$3.62、3.46%，至$108.23；WTI上漲$3.15、3.15%，至$103.20。市場焦點從可能的外交突破，轉向替代出口路線能否在庫存耗盡前重新啟用。

## 日本準備升息，印度著手回收流動性

日本8月企業物價年增7.6%，高於預估的7.4%，但低於7月修正值7.7%；月減0.2%，前期修正為月增0.4%。石油與煤製品、化學品、資訊通信設備及非鐵金屬，帶動年度漲幅。日圓計價進口價格仍年增24.8%，較修正後的29.3%放緩。

彭博調查的52名經濟學家全數預估9月18日日銀升息，93%預期1月前再升一次，約三分之一選擇12月，無人預估9月與10月連續升息。預估每季升息者占46%；認為維持六個月間隔者，則由7月的82%降至6%。終點利率預估中位數仍為1.75%。

路透訪問的四名知情人士指出，日銀可能升息25個基點至1.25%，接續6月升至1%的行動。但他們表示，央行沒有預設終點，委員會對後續速度也尚無共識；若通膨超標風險增加，不排除加快。週五日本10年期殖利率上升7.5個基點至2.985%，20年期上升7個基點至3.82%。澳洲3年期一度上升20個基點至5.05%，創2011年以來新高，10年期達5.38%。週五稍早交換市場估9月澳洲央行升息機率84%，高於週四的65%。這些亞洲交易發生在美國週五CPI之前，承接的是週四美債賣壓。

美國收盤後報導的Santander研究，則評估日本資金可能如何調整海外部位。Antonio Villarroya團隊估計，GPIF不必正式修改策略配置，就可能出售最多$620億美債。他們假設海外債券由25%目標降至允許的20%下限，並調整追蹤FTSE全球政府債券指數的方式。若日銀升息帶動日圓轉強，分析師認為這種情況更可能出現；GPIF並未宣布出售計畫。

印度央行宣布9月17日、21日及28日三次直接售債，合計₹1兆，首場涵蓋2029、2030、2031及2032年到期券。總裁Sanjay Malhotra此前表示，公開市場操作與外匯換匯均可使用，即使政策利率水準本身仍適當。

週三銀行體系剩餘流動性達₹10.49兆。特殊海外存款吸引約$1,270億，加計銀行與國有企業的補貼海外借款，相關措施共帶入$1,364億。隔夜利率跌破政策利率，暫時性流動性回收操作也未能持續消除落差。花旗估計，印度央行持有約₹23兆政府債，占中央政府證券18%，較前一財政年度高逾40%。

售債公告前，Malhotra談話已使10年期殖利率上升6個基點至7.035%，5年期一度上升10個基點至6.6222%。政府標售6.20%票息2029年券時，央行只接受₹450.6億，低於₹1,100億供給，得標殖利率6.4031%，交易員原估6.47%。6.57%票息2033年券及新2056年券，則分別售足原定₹1,100億與₹1,000億。空頭部位也增加，9月初5年期指標券每日借券超過₹1,000億，約為8月初兩倍。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership的Abhishek Upadhyay估計，週一假日後、週二恢復交易時，新售債計畫可能再推高10年期殖利率約10個基點，短端漲幅可能更大。

歐洲央行升息後，官員對後續各有側重。Joachim Nagel認為利率位於中性上緣，是否進入輕度限制區間，取決於能源；Ulo Kaasik認為市場反映後續升息可以理解，目前利率並不特別高；Gediminas Simkus強調通膨過高且可能持續，但未預測下次會議。拉加德在週六刊出的訪問中表示，中東衝突及煉油產能破壞、尤其俄羅斯的情況，使衝擊可能比先前預估更久，同時承認成長風險。

英國7月GDP月增0.4%，高於路透預估的持平；年增1.6%，創2025年2月以來最快，高於1.2%預估，三個月成長率也為0.4%。服務業、包括程式設計，是主要支撐，呼應Andrew Bailey所說的經濟比預期強。市場幾乎確定11月前升息，儘管多數經濟學家仍估9月不變。

俄羅斯維持利率14%，為2025年6月以來首次按兵不動；11名經濟學家中有三名原估降25個基點。煉油廠攻擊及燃料短缺推動通膨升至6.3%，央行警告，若9月底預算計畫的結構性初級赤字擴大，可能需要更緊政策。波蘭的Ludwik Kotecki則表示，只有預測顯示通膨持續高於4%，才可能在年底或明年初升息一至兩次、每次25個基點。他預期10月不變，11月新預測後再討論，與Adam Glapinski認為3.75%可維持至2027年中的看法不同。

巴西降息空間較大。8月IPCA月減0.32%，降幅大於預估的0.29%，為2022年8月以來最弱；年增率由4.44%降至4.22%，低於4.27%預估，並位於3%目標上下1.5個百分點的容許範圍內。住宅成本下降1.87%，受惠於Itaipu相關一次性電費折扣。經濟學家認為，這支持從14%再降25個基點，但不足以因暫時性利多加快寬鬆。

## 財政壓力下，法國有擔保債獲得不同評價

美國本財年前11個月赤字達$1.97兆，日曆調整後年減5%，其中8月赤字為$1,668億。支出$6.81兆、收入$4.85兆，調整後均增加3%。9月企業繳稅通常帶來盈餘，因此這尚非全年結果。

淨利息支出達$1兆，超過國防及多數主要支出，僅次於社會安全與衛生及公共服務部。隨低息債以更高利率再融資，可交易美債平均利率升至3.48%，比五年前高逾2個百分點。8月關稅收入為正$128億，此前因退還關稅，曾連續三個月出現淨減少。

法國放棄今年縮減赤字的努力，原先目標為GDP的5%，低於2025年的5.1%。Insee因消費疲弱、投資下滑，將成長預測由0.7%降至0.4%。法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin警告，2028年或2029年利息支出可能達€1,000億。

法國擔保債券的殖利率，目前比10年期政府債低近30個基點，四個月前兩者大致相當，倒掛幅度創紀錄。約€4,000億、占該市場四分之三的債券以房貸支持；優先順位、擔保品及付款保障，可使評等高於銀行或主權。UBS的Annalaura Capuano認為，這些評等優勢使持有人較能抵禦主權降評。不過，政府債交易更活躍、重新定價更快，公司債仍可能稍後轉弱，短天期的倒掛也較小。

週六，法國央行針對國會財政委員會主席Eric Coquerel質疑持債減少，澄清ECB購債計畫取得的證券並未在市場出售，並願向委員會說明。持有部位下降與主動賣債，因而是債務取消爭議中需要分清的兩件事。

塞內加爾完成宣布外債處理後的首次區域標售，募集CFA1,010億、約$1.79億，原定供給CFA1,000億，投標CFA1,090億。供給比8月28日多約43%，但5年期殖利率由8.24%降至7.89%；一年期國庫券平均7.87%，三年期公債7.75%。政府擬議的外債處理排除CFA計價債，使本地債需求與境外債談判有不同基礎。

匈牙利債務主管Gergely Tardos估計，歐元趨同可使長期福林殖利率降向4%，仍有150至250個基點空間。他也指出，投資人基礎擴大，納入持有期間更長的主權基金。這是新增的官方預估，並非已確定加入歐元區，或已實現的殖利率降幅。

## 股權連結融資創紀錄，公用事業發債卻卡在價格

美國上市公司可轉換證券募資已達$1,310億，8月貢獻$250億，使全年超越兩年前紀錄。高盛的Spencer Rogers估計，AI相關企業占發行44%，近30%新券不付票息。投資人願意為股價上行空間與波動性付費，讓企業即使面對接近5%的美債殖利率，也能保留現金。

這些工具的償還權利並不相同。Alphabet在6月發行兩部分、合計$205億強制轉換特別股，Oracle在2月發行$50億，均推高總額；強制轉換工具不像一般可轉債，讓持有人選擇到期收回現金本金。Nebius在8月宣布兩筆共$57.5億發行，CoreWeave與Iren也是主要發行人。Wells Fargo的Craig McCracken指出，波動率提高，使定價比一般債更具競爭力；較高轉換溢價也能減少相較於立即增資的稀釋。投資級發行人數較少，但平均交易規模遠大於非投資級。

Meta已連續至少一週與歐洲債券投資人會面，討論信用、策略與展望，但這是非交易路演，尚無發債委任或承諾。知情人士則表示，Microsoft因算力不足而被迫拒絕部分業務後，計畫將資料中心容量由約12 GW提高至2032年的逾38 GW。

週末AI安全聲明，為擴建步調增添變數。Anthropic的Dario Amodei提出包括獨立第三方評估的保障，並倡議放慢最先進模型開發。Sam Altman支持、Elon Musk也同意，Altman另稱OpenAI今年不會上市，以專注安全。週一早盤Nasdaq 100期貨下跌1.2%。摩根資產管理的Kerry Craig認為，在企業下修資本支出指引或延後模型推出之前，影響主要仍是情緒；目前聲明尚不能證明兩者已發生。

三菱日聯發行¥2,000億永續AT1，分為五年四個月及十年四個月後可贖回兩部分，分別加日本公債100及105個基點，均比4月窄5個基點，最終需求¥2,482億。相較之下，9月10日整體日圓投資級利差為47個基點，4月約45個基點，期間公司債發行超過¥10.7兆、創同期紀錄。較高票息與熟悉的大型銀行名稱，仍能在整體利差較寬時吸引買盤。

UBS宣布買回$79億原瑞信債券，為歷來最大一筆，使流通額由2023年接手時約$900億降至約$290億。其中一組上限先由$20億增至$40億，再增至$59億。CreditSights的Simon Adamson認為，這些資金不是已超出需求，就是相對昂貴。回收優先債有助降低融資成本，與遭減記AT1的訴訟是不同事項。

包括Santander、BNP Paribas、Barclays及UBS在內的十一家歐洲銀行主管，要求立即暫停增加資本要求。他們引用€2.5兆損失吸收能力，主張監管納入競爭力目標，並將較快的跨境整合措施與較慢的改革分開，兩者均於2027年初前提出。目前當局尚未同意放寬。

South East Water由NatWest安排的初步討論因價格停滯，儘管管理層稱有需求，董事會仍須重新考慮發行時點。King Street在7月同意為未來發行提供£2億出資保證，以避免先前預估明年8月出現的現金危機。公司槓桿率66.5%，高於Ofwat目標，近期供水、服務及信用評等問題，也帶來£3,050萬補償方案。

澳洲APRA則就Bathla曝險聯繫銀行與退休基金。開發商倒閉留下約A$34億債務，大多欠私人貸款人；監管機關表示，銀行直接曝險微不足道，退休基金直接部位也小，但仍強調受託人的投資治理與估值責任。檢視範圍不只直接貸款，也包括透過融資與投資形成的間接連結。

## 政策會議面對的，已是實際公布的通膨意外

9月16日聯準會決策、預測與記者會，將區分這是有限度回收先前降息，還是更持久的升息循環。CPI與通膨預期已意外走高，週五損益兩平下降、實質殖利率上升，則是Warsh說明需要多少限制力道時的市場起點。

9月16日決策前公布的零售銷售，預估增加0.9%，前期下降0.6%；同日還有進口物價，9月17日公布新屋開工與初領失業救濟金。9月15日20年期美債標售、9月17日10年期TIPS標售，將呈現名目與實質殖利率走高後的買盤需求。

英國9月15日薪資、9月16日通膨公布後，接著是9月17日英國央行決策及年度縮減持債公告。日本9月18日CPI與日銀會議，將顯示委員會是否支持經濟學家預期的更快步調，而不只同意下一次升息。印度9月14日通膨在本地市場休市時公布，週二將連同流動性回收計畫一起反映，之後9月17日進行首場售債。巴西9月16日則將決定，電費利多是否足以支持再小幅降息，而不加快整個循環。

在會議之前，沙烏地管線若部分重啟，可在延布庫存仍足夠時維持出口；若持續中斷，則使IEA下修後的供給展望更差，航運談判也仍延期。AI信用方面，實際支出修正、融資調整或模型延後，會比週末聲明帶來更持久的影響。兩者都可能在政策決策前，再次改變債市所面對的情勢。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Core inflation pushes the Fed closer to a hike

Treasuries flattened Friday as a stronger core-inflation reading brought a September Fed increase close to fully priced, while falling oil helped the long end recover. The 2-year yield rose 7 basis points to 4.63%, the 10-year added 1 to 4.96% and the 30-year fell 2 to 5.35%. By the end of a difficult week, 2-year yields were up 26 basis points and 10-years 18.

The inflation surprise was concentrated enough to leave room for debate, but not easily dismissed. Core CPI rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast; wireless charges contributed a record increase, while other services also strengthened. Michigan's survey then showed households expecting faster inflation even as confidence deteriorated. Futures put September hike odds around 90%, up from roughly 70%, with two increases priced by year-end.

Longer-dated pricing was less pessimistic. Ten-year breakevens fell 4 basis points to 2.36%, while real yields rose 5 to 2.60%. Oil's retreat helped equities and modestly tighter US investment-grade and high-yield spreads. Borrowers continued to find demand, from record convertible issuance to MUFG's tighter-priced bank capital, although South East Water could not agree terms with investors.

Weekend attacks and the prolonged Saudi pipeline outage subsequently reversed the energy relief at Monday's Asian opening. That leaves the coming policy meetings facing a renewed supply threat, after Friday's market had drawn some comfort from lower crude and a more forceful expected Fed response.

## A monthly CPI surprise outweighs the softer annual comparison

August headline CPI rose 0.4%, matching the Reuters poll after July's 0.1% increase; annual inflation held at 3.4%, also as expected. Core prices rose 0.3%, above both the 0.2% forecast and July's 0.2%, even as the annual core rate eased from 2.5% to 2.4%.

Energy rose 2.1%, groceries were little changed and owners' equivalent rent increased 0.2%. The more uncomfortable detail was a 0.5% advance in services excluding energy and rents. Wireless telephone charges recorded their largest increase, accompanied by strong hotel, motel and airfare gains. Core goods rose only 0.1%, led by new and used vehicles. Wireless pricing may explain a temporary part of the surprise, but pressure extended beyond that component.

Technology costs also stood out over the year: software and accessories rose a record 25.4%, and computers, peripherals and smart-home assistants a near-record 8.4%. Those increases bring the data-center investment boom's cost pressures into consumer-price data. Real average hourly earnings, meanwhile, fell 0.3% from August 2025, leaving household purchasing power under pressure.

Michigan's preliminary September sentiment index fell to 47.8 from 51.7, below the Reuters consensus of 51.0. One-year inflation expectations jumped from 4.0% to 4.6%; five-year expectations increased from 3.3% to 3.4%, above the 2.8%–3.2% range in 2024. Survey director Joanne Hsu cited fuel prices and trade tensions. Bloomberg's analysis found Republican confidence had erased most of its improvement since Trump's 2024 election victory. For the first time since 2023, a majority of consumers expected rates to rise over the next 12 months.

The 2-year yield initially reached 4.66%. Longer maturities subsequently recovered, leaving 2s10s 6 basis points narrower at 33 and 2s30s 9 narrower at 72. BMO's Ian Lyngen saw renewed confidence in the Fed's inflation response in the combination of front-end weakness and long-end strength. JPMorgan Asset Management's Priya Misra noted that markets had already incorporated much of a modest tightening cycle before the release.

Forecasters nevertheless shifted. TD Securities abandoned its call for no change throughout 2026 and now expects the first of three increases in September. JPMorgan and Nationwide also moved toward an imminent hike. Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic warned that oil, gasoline and diesel inflation could spread to other prices and expectations. Evercore ISI's Krishna Guha and colleagues judged the data insufficiently favorable for Kevin Warsh to look through another energy shock without risking credibility.

That reassessment followed a much more dovish pre-CPI survey. Only 13 of 48 economists in Bloomberg's September 4–9 poll expected a hike this month, and a majority forecast no change through end-2027. The Conference Board's Yelena Shulyatyeva had explicitly made her hold forecast conditional on inflation not decisively accelerating. Friday's data altered that condition.

White House messages changed after the close too. On Sunday, Trump again said the US should pay the world's lowest rates, said he did not know whether the Fed would hike, and reiterated that further trade restrictions could come over time. Kevin Hassett, who said Friday a hike would draw a presidential response, told CNN Sunday that the White House would support the committee. On Fox News Sunday, he said Trump would probably dislike an increase but defend Warsh's independence.

## Friday's oil decline gives way to a damaged export route

Brent fell 2.81% to $104.61 and WTI 2.37% to $100.05 at Friday's fixed-income close. Possible Gulf-Iran talks over Hormuz and an IEA demand downgrade offered relief. US stocks recovered after four losing sessions: the S&P 500 gained 0.86%, Nasdaq 100 0.91% and semiconductors 1.81%. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Crude nevertheless finished the week sharply higher, with Brent up 8.65% and WTI 9.37%.

The IEA cut supply as well as demand forecasts. It now expects world supply to contract 5.7 million barrels a day in 2026, about 6%, versus roughly 4% previously. August inventories fell 3.1 million barrels a day to levels last seen in 2023. Saudi supply dropped 2.3 million to 6 million barrels a day, its lowest in more than three decades, while OPEC+ production fell 1.8 million to 38.8 million. Full Gulf recovery was pushed into 2027.

Demand is adjusting to scarce, expensive fuel. The IEA widened its forecast 2026 consumption decline from 1.6 million to 2.5 million barrels a day, particularly as diesel prices restrain use. AAA's US diesel average reached a Friday record of $6.0556 a gallon. On-highway trucking accounts for about two-thirds of consumption, carrying that pressure into freight bills. Ukrainian attacks have reduced Russian diesel exports, and Middle Eastern refineries are still recovering from earlier strikes; crude availability alone does not resolve the processing bottleneck.

Asian fuel subsidies can transfer part of the burden to government finances. Emkay's Madhavi Arora estimated that a $10 Brent increase would theoretically add 35 basis points to Indian inflation and subtract 15 from growth, although diversification from Gulf supply could reduce the sensitivity this time. Thammasat University's Puree Sirasoontorn estimated Thailand's oil-fund deficit could rise from THB83 billion to around THB100 billion, potentially requiring government borrowing. These remain estimates of exposure, not spending already incurred.

Over the weekend, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remained closed. The route had carried about 4 million barrels a day to Yanbu, bypassing Hormuz. Buyers and traders told Reuters that an extended outage could remove as much as 4% of world supply. Three industry sources put Yanbu's export inventory cushion at five to seven days. Repair estimates ranged from five to six weeks to an earlier partial restart.

Saudi state media reported fresh Houthi strikes on Jazan and a nearby military base. A projectile hit a vessel in Hormuz, causing a fire and crew evacuation; Iran separately reported one death and four injuries on an Iranian commercial ship. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said Monday's planned Gulf-Iran meeting had been postponed, leaving discussion of a temporary shipping lane unresolved.

At 22:14 GMT Sunday, in early Monday Asian trading, Brent rose $3.62, or 3.46%, to $108.23, while WTI gained $3.15, or 3.15%, to $103.20. Attention had shifted from a possible diplomatic opening to whether an alternative export route could restart before its inventory cushion ran out.

## Japan prepares to tighten, India to remove liquidity

Japan's August corporate-goods prices rose 7.6% annually, above the 7.4% forecast but slower than July's revised 7.7%. Monthly prices fell 0.2% after revised July growth of 0.4%. Oil and coal products, chemicals, communications equipment and non-ferrous metals led the annual increase. Yen-based import prices remained 24.8% above a year earlier, easing from revised 29.3%.

All 52 economists in Bloomberg's survey expected a September 18 BOJ hike, and 93% another by January. About one-third chose December; none forecast consecutive September and October moves. Quarterly increases were expected by 46%, while the share forecasting six-month intervals fell to 6% from 82% in July. The median terminal-rate estimate stayed at 1.75%.

Reuters' four sources familiar with BOJ thinking pointed to a 25-basis-point move to 1.25%, following June's increase to 1%. They described no preset terminal rate or board agreement on the subsequent pace, while leaving faster action possible if overshoot risks grew. Friday's JGB market took 10-year yields up 7.5 basis points to 2.985% and 20-years up 7 to 3.82%. Australia's 3-year rose as much as 20 basis points to 5.05%, highest since 2011, and its 10-year reached 5.38%. Early Friday swaps put September RBA hike odds at 84%, up from Thursday's 65%. These sessions followed Thursday's US selloff and preceded Friday's CPI.

Santander research reported after the US close explored a possible overseas allocation response. Antonio Villarroya's team estimated GPIF could sell up to $62 billion of Treasuries without changing its strategic allocation. They modeled foreign bonds falling from the 25% target to the permitted 20% lower bound, alongside a change in how the fund tracks the FTSE World Government Bond Index. They saw this as more likely if BOJ tightening strengthened the yen; GPIF has not announced those sales.

India's RBI announced outright bond sales totaling ₹1 trillion on September 17, 21 and 28. The first operation covers 2029, 2030, 2031 and 2032 maturities. Governor Sanjay Malhotra had said both open-market operations and FX swaps were available, even while describing the policy-rate setting as appropriate.

The banking surplus reached ₹10.49 trillion Wednesday. Special foreign deposits attracted about $127 billion; including subsidized overseas borrowing by banks and state companies, the broader measures brought in $136.4 billion. Overnight rates fell below policy, and temporary reverse repos had not durably closed the gap. Citi estimated RBI government-bond holdings near ₹23 trillion, about 18% of central government securities and more than 40% above the prior fiscal-year level.

Before the sales announcement, the 10-year had risen 6 basis points to 7.035% after Malhotra's comments; the 5-year rose as much as 10 to 6.6222%. In the government's auction, RBI accepted only ₹45.06 billion of ₹110 billion offered in the 6.20% 2029, at a 6.4031% cutoff versus traders' 6.47% estimate. It sold the planned ₹110 billion 6.57% 2033 and ₹100 billion new 2056. Short positioning had grown, with daily borrowing of the 5-year benchmark above ₹100 billion in early September, about twice early August. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership's Abhishek Upadhyay estimated the new sales could add about 10 basis points to 10-year yields, and more at shorter maturities, when trading resumes Tuesday after Monday's holiday.

Europe's officials offered different emphases after the ECB hike. Joachim Nagel put rates at the upper end of neutral and allowed a move into mild restraint depending on energy. Ulo Kaasik called further market-priced hikes understandable and current rates not particularly high. Gediminas Simkus stressed excessive, potentially persistent inflation without forecasting the next meeting. In a Saturday interview, Christine Lagarde said the shock would probably last longer than previously expected, citing Middle Eastern conflict and destroyed refining capacity, especially in Russia, while acknowledging risks to growth.

Britain's July GDP rose 0.4% against a Reuters forecast of no change. Annual growth reached 1.6%, fastest since February 2025 and above 1.2% consensus; three-month growth was also 0.4%. Services, including programming, helped. The release supported Andrew Bailey's view that activity was firmer than expected. Markets saw a hike by November as nearly certain, although most economists expected September unchanged.

Russia held 14% for the first time since June 2025; three of 11 economists had expected a 25-basis-point cut. Inflation accelerated to 6.3%, with refinery attacks and shortages feeding prices. The bank warned that a larger structural primary deficit in budget plans due at September-end could require tighter policy. Poland's Ludwik Kotecki said one or two 25-basis-point hikes late this year or early next were possible only if forecasts showed inflation persistently above 4%. He expected October unchanged, then discussion after November projections, unlike Adam Glapinski's expectation of 3.75% through mid-2027.

Brazil offered more scope for easing. August IPCA fell 0.32%, versus a 0.29% decline forecast, its weakest month since August 2022. Annual inflation eased to 4.22% from 4.44%, below 4.27% consensus and inside the 3% target's 1.5-percentage-point band. Housing costs fell 1.87%, helped by a one-off Itaipu-linked electricity discount. Economists saw support for another measured 25-basis-point cut from 14%, rather than faster easing based on temporary relief.

## Fiscal pressure favors secured claims in France

The US deficit reached $1.97 trillion over the fiscal year's first 11 months, down 5% after calendar adjustments, including an August gap of $166.8 billion. Spending was $6.81 trillion and revenue $4.85 trillion, both up an adjusted 3%. September's corporate-tax deadlines often produce a surplus, so these are not full-year totals.

Net interest reached $1 trillion, exceeding defense and every major category except Social Security and Health and Human Services. The average rate on marketable Treasuries rose to 3.48%, more than 2 percentage points above five years earlier, as cheap debt refinanced at higher yields. August customs duties supplied $12.8 billion after three months of net declines associated with tariff refunds.

France abandoned its effort to reduce this year's deficit after targeting 5% of GDP versus 5.1% in 2025. Insee cut its growth forecast from 0.7% to 0.4% as consumption weakened and investment fell. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin warned interest costs could reach €100 billion in 2028 or 2029.

French covered bonds now yield almost 30 basis points less than 10-year sovereign debt, a record inversion from roughly equal yields four months ago. About €400 billion, three-quarters of the covered market, is mortgage-backed. Seniority, collateral and payment protections can support ratings above the bank or sovereign; UBS's Annalaura Capuano said those uplifts were insulating holders from potential sovereign downgrades. More actively traded government debt may also reprice sooner, leaving room for corporate debt to weaken later; shorter-maturity inversions are smaller.

On Saturday, the Bank of France clarified that none of its ECB-program holdings had been sold in the market, after finance-committee chair Eric Coquerel questioned a portfolio reduction. The bank offered to explain its operations. Falling holdings and active sales are therefore distinct in the continuing cancellation dispute.

Senegal completed its first regional auction since announcing external debt treatment, raising CFA101 billion, or $179 million, against a CFA100 billion offer and CFA109 billion bids. The offer was about 43% larger than August 28, but the 5-year yield fell from 8.24% to 7.89%; one-year bills averaged 7.87% and three-year bonds 7.75%. CFA debt is excluded from the proposed external exercise, preserving a different basis for local demand than for foreign-issued bonds.

Hungarian debt chief Gergely Tardos estimated euro convergence could bring long-term forint yields toward 4%, another 150–250 basis points lower. He reported a broader base including long-horizon sovereign funds. This adds an official estimate to the convergence case, rather than an agreed accession date or a realized yield decline.

## Record equity-linked funding contrasts with a stalled utility deal

US-listed companies have raised $131 billion in convertibles, surpassing the record set two years ago after August contributed $25 billion. Goldman Sachs's Spencer Rogers estimated AI-related issuers accounted for 44% of sales and nearly 30% of new bonds paid no coupon. Investors' willingness to pay for equity upside and volatility lets issuers conserve cash even with Treasury yields near 5%.

The total spans different repayment rights. Alphabet's $20.5 billion two-part mandatory convertible preferred offering in June and Oracle's $5 billion February deal helped drive it; mandatory instruments do not offer the usual cash-principal choice at maturity. Nebius announced $5.75 billion in two August issues, while CoreWeave and Iren were also major issuers. Wells Fargo's Craig McCracken said volatility made pricing more competitive with straight debt. High conversion premiums reduce dilution relative to immediate equity sales. Fewer investment-grade issuers bring much larger average deals than sub-investment-grade borrowers.

Meta has spent at least a week meeting European bond investors about its credit, strategy and outlook on a non-deal roadshow, without a mandate or offering commitment. Microsoft plans to expand data-center capacity from about 12 gigawatts to over 38 by 2032, according to people familiar, after shortages forced it to turn away business.

Weekend safety statements introduced uncertainty over the pace of that buildout. Anthropic's Dario Amodei proposed safeguards including independent evaluations and slower frontier-model development. Sam Altman supported the proposal, Elon Musk agreed, and Altman said OpenAI would not list this year so it could focus on safety. Early Monday Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.2%. JPMorgan Asset Management's Kerry Craig saw mainly a sentiment effect until companies cut capex guidance or delay releases; neither is established by the statements alone.

MUFG priced ¥200 billion perpetual AT1 in tranches callable after five years and four months and ten years and four months. Margins were 100 and 105 basis points over government bonds, both 5 tighter than April, with ¥248.2 billion final demand. By contrast, broader yen IG spreads were 47 basis points September 10 versus about 45 in April, amid record period issuance above ¥10.7 trillion. Higher coupons and a familiar megabank attracted demand despite wider spreads elsewhere.

UBS announced a $7.9 billion legacy Credit Suisse bond purchase, its largest, leaving about $29 billion outstanding from roughly $90 billion at the 2023 takeover. One group's maximum rose from $2 billion to $4 billion and then $5.9 billion. CreditSights' Simon Adamson described the funding as surplus or relatively expensive. These senior retirements reduce funding costs and remain separate from litigation over written-off AT1.

Executives at eleven European banks, including Santander, BNP Paribas, Barclays and UBS, requested an immediate moratorium on capital increases. Citing €2.5 trillion loss-absorbing capacity, they sought a supervisory competitiveness mandate and faster cross-border integration measures, separate from slower reforms, with both presented by early 2027. Authorities have not granted the requested relief.

South East Water's initial NatWest-led discussions stalled over price. The board will reconsider issuance timing despite management describing investor demand. King Street's July agreement supplies a £200 million backstop for a future sale, intended to avert a cash crunch previously expected next August. Gearing of 66.5% exceeds Ofwat's target, and supply, service and rating problems recently led to a £30.5 million redress package.

APRA contacted Australian banks and pension funds over Bathla exposure after the developer's collapse left about A$3.4 billion owed, mostly to private lenders. Direct bank exposure was negligible and superannuation exposure small, the regulator said, while emphasizing trustee governance and valuations. The inquiry follows the indirect funding and investment connections as well as direct loans.

## Policy meetings now face realized inflation surprises

The September 16 Fed meeting, projections and press conference must distinguish a limited reversal of earlier easing from a more persistent tightening cycle. CPI and expectations have now surprised higher. Friday's lower breakevens and higher real yields provide the starting point for Warsh's explanation of how much restraint is needed.

Retail sales, due September 16 before the decision, are forecast to rise 0.9% after a 0.6% decline. Import prices follow the same day; housing starts and claims arrive September 17. The September 15 20-year Treasury auction and September 17 10-year TIPS sale will show demand at higher nominal and real yields.

UK wages on September 15 and inflation September 16 precede the September 17 BoE decision and annual bond-reduction announcement. Japan's September 18 CPI and BOJ decision will show whether the board endorses the faster pace now expected by economists, not just the next hike. India's September 14 inflation arrives during the local market holiday; Tuesday trading must absorb it alongside announced liquidity withdrawal, before September 17's first sale. Brazil's September 16 decision will test whether electricity relief permits another small cut without accelerating the cycle.

Before those meetings, a partial Saudi pipeline restart could preserve exports while Yanbu inventories last. A prolonged outage would deepen the IEA's supply downgrade, with shipping talks postponed. In AI credit, actual spending revisions, financing changes or model delays would matter more durably than weekend statements. Both could alter the outlook before policymakers announce their decisions.

overall_summary.headline: Core CPI pushes up the front end as oil relief supports long bonds
overall_summary.session_narrative: September Fed hike odds rose from roughly 70% to 90%, with two increases priced by year-end. Ten-year real yields rose 5 basis points to 2.60%, while breakevens fell 4 to 2.36%, leaving nominal yields only 1 basis point higher at 4.96%. The market was pricing more restraint rather than uniformly higher long-run inflation. Corporate demand remained selective: convertibles set a record and MUFG tightened AT1 pricing, but South East Water's investor discussions stalled over price. Monday's Asian oil rebound belongs to the subsequent Saudi pipeline and shipping disruption, not Friday's close.
overall_summary.summary: The 2-year yield rose 7 basis points to 4.63% after core CPI beat forecasts and household inflation expectations climbed. The 30-year fell 2 basis points to 5.35% as Friday's oil retreat helped long duration, equities and modest spread tightening. Weekend supply disruptions then reversed crude's relief before the coming policy meetings.
